Land Buying Checklist: What to Look for Before You Make an Offer

Before you write an offer on that dream piece of Colorado land, make sure you’ve checked all the boxes. Use this guide as a quick-reference checklist for evaluating rural property — from utilities to access to zoning.

Water: Well or Tap?

  • Is there a well permit or a city/rural water tap?
  • Has the water been tested recently?
  • What type of well permit (household-use only or domestic)?

Septic System

  • Is there an existing septic system?
  • Request past pumping or maintenance records
  • Has it been inspected (or required) in your county?

Access and Roads

  • Is access legal, year-round, and recorded?
  • Are there private road maintenance agreements?
  • Drive the road in different weather if possible

Zoning and Setbacks

  • What is the property zoned for?
  • Can you build a shop, barn, or accessory dwelling?
  • What are the required setbacks?

Utilities

  • How far is electricity from the build site?
  • Is internet available (wired, wireless, or satellite)?
  • Will you need propane or is natural gas an option?

Surveys and Boundaries

  • Is there a recent survey or ILC?
  • Check fences, structures, and easements for accuracy

Other Considerations

  • Is the land in a floodplain, wildfire zone, or steep slope area?
  • Ask about nearby agriculture, animals, or odor/noise factors
  • Get insurance quotes if in a high-risk area
